title: Warm-start probing and dashboard runbook
content:
TL;DR:
This is a compact runbook + lab notes for measuring and surfacing warm-start health for tokenized inference paths. Focus is on short probes that exercise prefix warm cache, controller decisions, and GPU warm-start variability across tenants. Purpose: get repeatable signals, low-cardinality dashboard, and a minimal on-call checklist to triage warm-start regressions.

Goals:
- Define 3–6 high-signal metrics for warm-start behavior (fast to compute, low cost to store).
- Add trace anchors so operator can link warm-start anomalies to model/runtime events.
- Prototype 1 micro-dashboard (2 rows) and 3 microcards for oncall.
- Run a 3-week experiment to evaluate sampling and alert thresholds.

Context and motivation (notes):
- Several customer incidents flagged slow first-token responses after bursty traffic — likely warm-start variance on shards and KV cache coldness.
- Existing dashboards capture overall latency but conflate cold-starts, IO stalls, and long-tail model decode issues. We need a focused lens on the warm path.
- Keep signal set small to limit costs and make SLO guardrails operational.

Metric definitions (precise):
1) warm_probe_success_rate (percent): numerator = probes with first-token latency < 120ms and no retry path; denominator = total probes executed. Unit: percent. Cardinality: global + region. Aggregation: rolling 5m and 1h.
2) prefix_warmth_latency_median_ms: median(first-token-latency) for requests where prefix_cache_hit = true AND probe_tag = warm_probe. Tagging: prefix_length_bucket: [0-32,33-128,129-512].
3) warm_tail_95p_ms and warm_tail_99p_ms: 95th/99th percentiles restricted to warm probe traces (sample 100% for probes, see tracing policy).
4) kv_prefix_hit_rate_by_len: fraction of requests where prefix_kv_hit = true per prefix_length_bucket. Helpful to see eviction thresholds.
5) warm_concurrency_ratio: hot_workers_processing_warm_requests / total_workers_processing_requests (gives clue if warm requests get queued).
6) probe_error_reason_counts: counts by error_reason labels: {cache_miss, eviction_race, backend_oom, rpc_timeout}.

How to collect probes:
- Lightweight probe inserted in router before model selection; probes are synthetic short-prompts (3–12 tokens) routed with low priority but same placement logic as real user traffic.
- Probes are tagged with trace field probe=true and probe_id. Probes rotate across prefix lengths.
- Probe cadence: 1 probe / shard / minute in canary regions; 1 probe / shard / 5 minutes globally during experiment.

Tracing strategy (span/annotation schema):
- Span names: router.probe -> placement.evaluate -> model.init_warm -> model.decode.first_token -> model.decode.total
- Add span attributes: probe=true, probe_id, prefix_len, kv_cache_hit (true|false), shard_id, gpu_uuid, model_version, quant_profile
- Critical trace anchors: when model.init_warm takes >50ms, capture stack snapshot tag (lightweight), record eviction metadata (evicted_keys_count).
- Sampling: keep 100% traces for probes. For production traffic, use severity sampling: keep 100% when first-token latency > 95th percentile OR when prefix_kv_hit=false and latency > 75th. Otherwise 2% baseline.

Dashboard wireframe (micro-dashboard):
Row A (health):
- Card 1: warm_probe_success_rate (5m sparkline + current) with region filter
- Card 2: kv_prefix_hit_rate_by_len (stacked bars by prefix_length_bucket)
Row B (investigation):
- Card 3: warm_tail_95p_ms / warm_tail_99p_ms (time series)
- Card 4: probe_error_reason_counts (top 5 reasons) + links to latest traces
- Small panel: warm_concurrency_ratio and active_probe_count (for surge detection)
Notes: use low-cardinality labels; provide a link from each card to a trace query (trace filter: probe=true AND prefix_len_bucket=selected).

Alerting and thresholds (proposal):
- P0 alert (oncall page): warm_probe_success_rate < 85% globally for 15m OR warm_tail_99p_ms > 2s for 10m. Pager if sustained for 30m.
- P1 (pageless): kv_prefix_hit_rate_by_len for 33-128 drops > 20pp baseline for 30m (notify slack #obs-warmstart).
- Alert rationale: P0 tied to customer-impacting first-token regressions; P1 is early-warning for cache churn.

Experiment plan (phased):
Phase 0 (week 0): implement probe tagging + trace span changes behind feature flag. Smoke tests in staging.
Phase 1 (weeks 1–2): Canary region probes + dashboard prototype. Run 100% tracing for probes. Collect baseline for 7 days.
Phase 2 (weeks 3–5): Expand to all regions at reduced cadence. Start alerting on P1.
Phase 3 (week 6): If stable, flip to continuous monitoring; add retention for probe metrics 90 days and trace retention 30 days for probe traces.

Oncall quick checklist (for first responder):
1) Confirm probe success_rate on micro-dashboard and check region breakdown.
2) Open trace link (from card) for several 99p traces and inspect span model.init_warm and decode.first_token timestamps.
3) Identify if kv_cache_hit=false correlates with high latency. If yes, check eviction logs and recent autoscaler events.
4) If model.init_warm spans show GPU contention (init > 100ms) cross-check GPU utilization and preemption events.
5) If nothing obvious, escalate to runtime team and attach 3 traces + summary.

Acceptance criteria for rollout:
- Warm_probe_success_rate >= 92% in all production regions for 7 consecutive days post-rollback window OR
- When success rate below threshold, cause attributable to a known, fixable change (e.g., eviction policy tweak), and mitigated within 48hrs.

Storage and cost considerations (notes):
- Metric retention: keep warm metrics rolled up to 1h for 90 days, raw 5m for 14 days.
- Trace retention: keep probe traces 30 days; compress and archive tails beyond 30d to cold storage for 1 year.
- Limit high-cardinality tags: avoid user_id, tenant_id — use tenant_bucket (low-cardinality) only if needed for enterprise debugging.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: Should probes attempt to pre-warm KV cache proactively on a per-tenant basis? Risk: can amplify eviction churn.
- Q: What is appropriate probe prompt set to mimic real-world prefix distributions? Action: Lina to sample 1000 recent short requests and propose probe corpus.
- TODO: Marcus to draft the instrumentation PR for span attributes (ENG-2321).
- TODO: Add integration tests to ensure probe tracing does not add >2ms to router path.

Notes to self / shorthand (incomplete):
- Keep probe volume small to avoid skewing autoscaler metrics. Gate by traffic percentile.
- When tuning alerts, test via synthetic pressure (staging) and verify noise rate <= 1 per week.

References and links:
- Confluence spec (linked_artifacts) for longer writeup.
- Observability cost calculator (internal sheet) to estimate incremental ingest.
- Related incident: INC-2025-warm-token-tail (see linked Artifacts).

If you take this on: start by enabling probe flag in staging, then run Phase 0 checklist. Ping me (Aisha) in #obs-warmstart for reviews.
